Physical measurement of the egg can be expressed by mass. The number of eggs necessary to get a reliable estimate of egg mass depends strongly on the weight of the eggs. With individual egg dry weight in the range of 3-5 µg, we recommend to pool at least 20 eggs. For larger eggs one can obtain individual dry weight measurement (Moretti et al (2016) (SupplMat, p28-30))

Physical measurement of the egg can be expressed by volume. To get a reliable estimate of egg volume, at least 5-10 randomly chosen eggs should be collected per clutch or per female. Eggs can best be photographed using a digital camera connected to a stereomicroscope, as direct measurement with an ocular micrometer is less precise. For spherical eggs it suffices to measure the diameter (d) of the egg and calculate volume according to the equation V = (pid3)/6. When eggs are of an ellipsoid shape, volume can often be approximated as two joint cones according to the equation V = 2/3pi*(L/2)*((w/2)2), where L is egg length and w is egg width (Moretti et al (2016) (SupplMat, p28-30))
